evals.name: scaffold-new-context-standard
evals.prompt: This Rust workspace `loyalty` follows the rust-ddd standard (variant: standard; contexts already present: `member`, `kernel` crate exists). Add a bounded context `reward` with an aggregate Reward (id, customer_id, points, status ACTIVE/REDEEMED/EXPIRED), a use case for a customer to redeem a reward, a back-office query that lists a customer's rewards, a Postgres repository with read-replica support, and a Redis cache for Reward. Produce the full file tree with file names only (no bodies) and state which architecture check would catch each common mistake.
evals.expected_output: A new crate crates/reward (named after the context) with Cargo.toml, migrations/<timestamp>_create_reward_tables.sql (tables prefixed reward_, no FK into member's tables), and src/: lib.rs (private `mod domain; mod application; mod infrastructure; mod presentation;`, `wire(RewardDeps) -> Reward` handle, `migrate(&PgPool)` with set_ignore_missing, RewardDeps with pool, replica: Option<PgPool>, Clock, IdGenerator; RewardConfig only if config exists; no `pub use application::published` unless another context calls in), domain.rs, domain/reward.rs (aggregate root Reward + RewardId = Id<Reward> + Customer marker/CustomerId + re-exports) and domain/reward/{reward_status.rs, reward_repository.rs (find_by_id, find_by_id_readonly, save; #[cfg(test)] fakes), reward_cache.rs, events.rs (RewardRedeemed, #[must_use]), error.rs (RewardError implementing ErrorCode)}; application.rs, application/client/{redeem_reward.rs (RedeemRewardUseCase + RedeemRewardInput + RedeemRewardError), output.rs (RewardOutput + From<&Reward>)}, application/management/{reward_management_query.rs (RewardManagementQueryUseCase + RewardManagementQueryRepository trait), output.rs (RewardListItemOutput)}; infrastructure/repository/{pg_reward_repository.rs (private RewardRow, primary + replica pools), pg_reward_management_query_repository.rs}, infrastructure/cache/redis_reward_cache.rs; presentation/web/reward_client.rs (RewardClientHandlers + routes) and presentation/rpc/reward_management.rs (RewardManagementHandlers). Rust 2018 module files, no mod.rs. The binary's bootstrap adds reward::migrate and reward::wire, and the architecture test's `contexts` gains "reward" (A-01 reports an unlisted crate). `redis` is denied in application and presentation. Mistakes mapped to checks: ports/ or types/ or config/ modules -> A-06; mod.rs -> A-07; pub mod or extra pub items at the crate root -> A-01; *Impl/*Adapter/*Port names -> A-10; cache named without a tech prefix -> A-11; application importing infrastructure -> A-02; sqlx in domain or application -> A-04; pub fields or set_status on Reward -> A-12; Option id -> A-13; event without #[must_use] -> A-14; Utc::now in domain -> A-05.

evals.name: scaffold-small-variant-single-context
evals.prompt: A single-crate Rust app `grimoire` (axum + sqlx Postgres) catalogs works stored on a NAS and fetches metadata candidates from DLsite and VNDB. It adopts rust-ddd, variant: small, and has one bounded context. Lay out src/ (file names only) for: a Work aggregate with tags; a job that scans the NAS directory and registers new works; looking up metadata candidates from DLsite and VNDB; an HTTP API to list works and confirm a metadata candidate for a work. Say explicitly where the SQL, the DLsite/VNDB HTTP clients, the NAS directory walker, and configuration loading go.
evals.expected_output: Single-context small variant: the four layers sit directly under src/ beside main.rs, lib.rs (mod declarations, pub use bootstrap::run), bootstrap.rs (AppConfig via envy/dotenvy, sqlx::migrate!() over one migrations/ dir, wiring, serve), kernel.rs + kernel/ (pub(crate), fakes under #[cfg(test)], http module). domain/work.rs (aggregate root Work, WorkId = Id<Work>) with domain/work/{tag.rs or work_tag.rs value object, work_repository.rs, metadata_source.rs (trait returning domain-language candidates), library_source.rs or another trait for the NAS listing, events.rs, error.rs}; behavior such as Work::confirm_metadata(candidate, at) -> Result<Event, WorkError>. application split by scenario/actor: application/client/{work_client_query.rs, confirm_work_metadata.rs, find_metadata_candidates.rs or similar, output.rs} and a job-only scenario module (application/library_scan/ or scan/) holding ScanLibraryUseCase. infrastructure/repository/pg_work_repository.rs (+ WorkRow) and pg_work_client_query_repository.rs hold all SQL; infrastructure/acl/dlsite/dlsite_metadata_source_acl.rs and acl/vndb/vndb_metadata_source_acl.rs hold the reqwest clients and translate into domain types; infrastructure/storage/fs_library_source.rs (Fs prefix) holds the walkdir/spawn_blocking walker; infrastructure/scheduling/ triggers the scan job if it runs periodically. presentation/web/work_client.rs with WorkClientHandlers calls use cases only: no SQL, no tokio::fs, no reqwest in handlers (A-04 denies sqlx/reqwest in presentation). Configuration is read only in bootstrap and passed through wire; no config module, no env::var in context code (A-05). Ids are typed, entities have private fields (no plain-data pub-field structs). tests/architecture/ with Variant::Small and empty contexts.

evals.name: review-deviations-standard
evals.prompt:
Review this rust-ddd (variant: standard) context listing and report every deviation with its rule id and a one-line fix.

crates/billing/src/lib.rs: `pub mod domain; mod application; mod infrastructure; mod presentation; pub fn wire(..)`
crates/billing/src/domain/mod.rs
crates/billing/src/domain/subscription/mod.rs: `pub struct Subscription { pub id: Option<SubscriptionId>, pub status: SubscriptionStatus }` with `pub fn set_status(&mut self, s: SubscriptionStatus)`
crates/billing/src/domain/subscription/types.rs: `BillingPeriod`, `Money`
crates/billing/src/domain/subscription/events.rs: `#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)] pub struct SubscriptionRenewed { .. }`
crates/billing/src/domain/subscription/renewer.rs: `SubscriptionRenewer::renew(&self, pool: &sqlx::PgPool)` which calls `chrono::Utc::now()`
crates/billing/src/application/ports/subscription_port.rs: `#[async_trait] pub trait SubscriptionPort`
crates/billing/src/application/ports/unit_of_work.rs: `trait UnitOfWork { async fn begin(&self) -> sqlx::Transaction<'static, Postgres>; }`
crates/billing/src/application/use_cases/renew_subscription.rs: `pub struct RenewSubscription` with `pub async fn execute(..) -> anyhow::Result<()>` and `pub async fn handle(&self, e: InvoicePaid)`
crates/billing/src/application/use_cases/start_subscription.rs: calls `catalog::published::PlanQueries::find_plan` directly from the use case
crates/billing/src/application/use_cases/subscription_helper.rs: `pub struct SubscriptionHelper`
crates/billing/src/infrastructure/postgres/subscription_repo.rs: `pub struct SubscriptionRepositoryImpl` implementing `SubscriptionPort`; `#[derive(sqlx::FromRow)]` added on the domain `Subscription`
crates/billing/src/infrastructure/config.rs: reads `std::env::var("PERIOD_DAYS")`
crates/billing/src/presentation/web/handlers.rs: an axum handler that runs `sqlx::query("UPDATE billing_subscriptions ...")` itself
crates/billing/migrations/20261001_create.sql: `plan_code TEXT REFERENCES catalog_plans(code)`
evals.expected_output: Exhaustive list by rule id: R-01/A-01 `pub mod domain` in lib.rs -> private `mod domain`. R-08/A-07 domain/mod.rs and subscription/mod.rs -> domain.rs, subscription.rs (concept file is the aggregate root). R-15/A-12 pub fields and set_status -> private fields, getters, a named behavior returning Result<Event, Error>. R-16/A-13 Option<SubscriptionId> -> id from construction via IdGenerator in application. R-07/A-06 domain types.rs -> billing_period.rs in subscription/, money.rs at domain root; application ports/ and use_cases/ -> scenario/actor modules (client/...); infrastructure postgres/ and config.rs -> repository/, configuration via wire; presentation handlers.rs -> module per scenario+actor (R-27). R-17/A-14 SubscriptionRenewed lacks #[must_use]. R-06/A-05 Utc::now in domain -> take at: Timestamp; env::var in infrastructure -> AppConfig in the binary, BillingConfig through wire (D-WS-07). R-05/A-04 sqlx in domain (renewer) -> repository trait; sqlx in application (UnitOfWork) and presentation (handler SQL) -> denied; anyhow in application -> thiserror RenewSubscriptionError implementing ErrorCode (R-23). R-09 traits in application/ports -> domain beside the concept, named for the need (SubscriptionRepository). R-13/A-10 SubscriptionPort, SubscriptionRepositoryImpl, SubscriptionHelper -> banned suffixes. R-14/A-11 SubscriptionRepositoryImpl -> PgSubscriptionRepository in infrastructure/repository/. R-11/A-08 RenewSubscription mixes execute and handle -> a separate event-driven use case for InvoicePaid; also name *UseCase with *Input. R-19 UnitOfWork / Transaction through a trait -> intent-named single-method trait (e.g. RenewalRecorder) whose adapter owns the transaction. R-04/A-03 start_subscription calls catalog::published directly -> billing domain trait PlanSource + infrastructure/acl/catalog/CatalogPlanSourceAcl. R-25 FromRow on the domain Subscription -> private SubscriptionRow + TryFrom via from_persisted. R-12/R-27 handler running SQL -> call one use case. R-26 FK into catalog_plans -> plain value reference, no cross-context FK. Each item cites its rule id; passing rules are not listed.

evals.name: naming
evals.prompt: Using the rust-ddd naming standard, name these for a `catalog` context and say where each lives: (1) a domain component that decides whether a Plan may be offered in a country; (2) one that computes a prorated price; (3) the Redis implementation of PlanCache; (4) the implementation that gets a customer's tier from the customer context; (5) the persistence row for the plans table and the Postgres repository; (6) the conversion from the Plan aggregate to its Output; (7) the trait other contexts use to look plans up, and what implements it; (8) a test double for PlanRepository; (9) the handler module and state for back-office plan management. Also list the banned names and why.
evals.expected_output: (1) PlanAvailabilityGuard or PlanOfferingPolicy (agent noun / Policy) in domain/plan/, not PlanService/PlanManager; (2) ProrationCalculator in domain/plan/ (or a proration/ sub-concept); (3) RedisPlanCache in infrastructure/cache/; (4) a catalog domain trait such as CustomerTierSource implemented by an `...Acl` type (e.g. CustomerTierSourceAcl) in infrastructure/acl/customer/, calling customer::published; (5) private PlanRow inside infrastructure/repository/pg_plan_repository.rs, PgPlanRepository; (6) impl From<&Plan> for PlanOutput in the scenario's output.rs, not PlanMapper/PlanConverter (an OutputAssembler only when gathering from collaborators); (7) PlanQueries in application/published.rs, implemented directly by the query use case (PlanClientQueryUseCase), re-exported via `pub use application::published`; (8) FakePlanRepository in a #[cfg(test)] pub(crate) mod fakes inside plan_repository.rs; (9) presentation/rpc/plan_management.rs with PlanManagementHandlers. Banned: *Impl, *Adapter, *Port, *Mapper, *Converter, *Dto, *Po, *Dao, *Entity, *Vo, *TransactionalWriter, *DomainService everywhere; *Manager, *Helper, *Util(s) in domain and application; reasons: technique words instead of domain words, or too general to name a responsibility.

evals.name: atomic-write-and-events
evals.prompt: In the billing context (rust-ddd, standard), settling an invoice must mark the invoice paid and extend its subscription by one period atomically. Afterwards a separate `notification` context, running in the same process, must react to the settlement. Show where each step lives (layer, file, type), which traits are involved, where the transaction opens and closes, and how the event reaches the notification context.
evals.expected_output: Domain: Invoice::settle(&mut self, at) -> Result<InvoiceSettled, InvoiceError> and Subscription::extend(&mut self, at) -> Result<SubscriptionExtended, SubscriptionError> (time passed in, events #[must_use] + Serialize). A single-method intent-named trait at the domain root, e.g. SettlementRecorder::record(&invoice, &subscription) (no UnitOfWork, no Transaction in any signature). Application: SettleInvoiceUseCase in the owning scenario loads both aggregates, reads clock.now() once, calls both behaviors, calls the recorder, then publishes through DomainEventPublisher (trait at the domain root taking a BillingEvent enum built with From impls) because a consumer now exists; publishing happens after persistence. Infrastructure: PgSettlementRecorder in infrastructure/repository/ opens pool.begin(), writes both through shared executor helpers, commits; InMemoryDomainEventPublisher in infrastructure/event/ translates the domain event into billing's published message type (e.g. published::InvoiceSettledMessage) and sends it on a tokio broadcast channel. Wiring: billing's wire handle exposes the sender/subscription; the binary passes it into NotificationDeps; notification's wire subscribes and spawns infrastructure/acl/billing/InvoiceSettledConsumer (it names billing::published, so it lives under acl/, A-03), which translates the published message into its own *Input and calls its event-driven use case's single handle(input). Delivery over broadcast is at most once; an outbox would be a new decision. The domain struct never crosses the context boundary.

evals.name: cross-context-call
evals.prompt: In a rust-ddd standard workspace, billing must read a plan's monthly price from catalog when a customer subscribes. Produce the catalog side (what is exposed and how), the billing side (traits, ACL, files), the Cargo dependency, how a catalog error or a missing plan is handled, and the order of wiring in the binary.
evals.expected_output: Catalog: application/published.rs declares `pub trait PlanQueries` (find_plan(&str) -> Result<PlanOutput, PlanQueryError>) and re-exports PlanOutput and PlanQueryError (pub, no internal types inside: storage failures become Unavailable(Box<dyn Error>)); implemented directly by PlanClientQueryUseCase; lib.rs has `pub use application::published;` and wire returns Catalog { router, plans: Arc<dyn PlanQueries> }. Billing: domain trait PlanSource beside the subscription concept (find_price(&PlanCode) -> Result<Option<Money>, PlanSourceError>) using billing's own PlanCode and Money; infrastructure/acl/catalog/catalog_plan_source_acl.rs CatalogPlanSourceAcl translates exhaustively (NotFound/InvalidCode -> Ok(None), Unavailable -> PlanSourceError::Unavailable); published enums are not #[non_exhaustive] so new variants force the ACL to decide. StartSubscriptionUseCase depends on Arc<dyn PlanSource>, not on catalog. billing/Cargo.toml depends on catalog; BillingDeps carries plans: Arc<dyn catalog::published::PlanQueries>; A-03 rejects catalog:: paths outside infrastructure/acl/ and lib.rs. Binary: catalog::migrate then billing::migrate; catalog::wire first, then billing::wire with catalog.plans; merge routers. Cargo forbids a cycle back from catalog to billing. No FK from billing tables to catalog tables.
